structural-causal.name: power-to-compute bottleneck conversion
structural-causal.basis: controlled energized sites can shorten AI infrastructure deployment, but value capture depends on GPU availability, energization and contract economics

discovery-weak-signals.name: AI infrastructure conversion
discovery-weak-signals.basis: contracted GPU capacity and expanded powered footprint indicate conversion from mining/power assets toward AI infrastructure

adversarial-red-team.name: capital intensity and earnings-quality risk
adversarial-red-team.basis: rapid AI/HPC expansion occurs while consolidated gross economics are weak, raising financing and execution sensitivity

expectations-execution.name: financial execution
expectations-execution.basis: strong revenue and adjusted EBITDA improvement coexist with negative gross margin and a wider net loss

items.risk: AI contracts depend on facility energization, GPU deployment and customer performance; Bhutan expansion is only an LOI.
Rapid AI/HPC buildout while core economics are volatile can increase funding and execution risk.
Successor bottlenecks can migrate from power/site access to GPUs, networking, cooling, financing or customer credit quality.
Customer concentration, GPU obsolescence, power-price exposure and financing needs can erode headline contracted-revenue value.
Bhutan expansion described as an LOI should not be treated as equivalent to contracted/operating capacity.
